requirements.quote:
The following discussion assumes that
   the name server is authoritative for the zone that would have held
   the non-existent RRsets matching SNAME.  The algorithm below is
   written for clarity, not for efficiency.

   To find the NSEC that proves that no RRsets matching name N exist in
   the zone Z that would have held them, construct a sequence, S,
   consisting of the owner names of every RRset in Z, sorted into



Arends, et al.              Standards Track                    [Page 13]


RFC 4035             DNSSEC Protocol Modifications            March 2005


   canonical order ([RFC4034]), with no duplicate names.
requirements.condition: In the described conceptual algorithm, when an authoritative name server finds an NSEC RR proving that no RRsets with owner name N exist in its zone Z.
requirements.required_behavior: The conceptual lookup sequence S contains the owner names of every RRset in zone Z.
requirements.why_checkable: The owner names considered by NSEC lookup can be compared with the complete set of RRset owner names in the authoritative zone; the conceptual algorithm does not prescribe a physical sequence representation.

requirements.condition: In the described conceptual algorithm, when an authoritative name server finds an NSEC RR proving that no RRsets with owner name N exist in its zone Z.
requirements.required_behavior: Order the conceptual sequence S of zone RRset owner names in canonical order as referenced by RFC4034.
requirements.why_checkable: The ordering used for predecessor lookup can be checked against canonical owner-name order without requiring the implementation to materialize the conceptual sequence.

   To find the NSEC that proves that no RRsets matching name N exist in
   the zone Z that would have held them, construct a sequence, S,
   consisting of the owner names of every RRset in Z, sorted into



Arends, et al.              Standards Track                    [Page 13]


RFC 4035             DNSSEC Protocol Modifications            March 2005


   canonical order ([RFC4034]), with no duplicate names.  Find the name
   M that would have immediately preceded N in S if any RRsets with
   owner name N had existed.
requirements.condition: In the described conceptual algorithm, when an authoritative name server finds an NSEC RR proving that no RRsets with owner name N exist in its zone Z.
requirements.required_behavior: Find M as the owner name that would immediately precede N in the canonical, duplicate-free sequence S if RRsets with owner name N existed.
requirements.why_checkable: For an absent target name and known ordered zone names, the selected predecessor M is a concrete value that can be checked.

requirements.quote:
The following discussion assumes that
   the name server is authoritative for the zone that would have held
   the non-existent RRsets matching SNAME.  The algorithm below is
   written for clarity, not for efficiency.

   To find the NSEC that proves that no RRsets matching name N exist in
   the zone Z that would have held them, construct a sequence, S,
   consisting of the owner names of every RRset in Z, sorted into



Arends, et al.              Standards Track                    [Page 13]


RFC 4035             DNSSEC Protocol Modifications            March 2005


   canonical order ([RFC4034]), with no duplicate names.  Find the name
   M that would have immediately preceded N in S if any RRsets with
   owner name N had existed.  M is the owner name of the NSEC RR that
   proves that no RRsets exist with owner name N.
requirements.condition: In the described conceptual algorithm, when an authoritative name server finds an NSEC RR proving that no RRsets with owner name N exist in its zone Z.
requirements.required_behavior: Select the NSEC RR owned by M, the owner name that would immediately precede N in S, as the proof that no RRsets exist with owner name N.
requirements.why_checkable: The returned denial-of-existence record owner can be compared with the predecessor computed for the absent target name.

requirements.quote:
The algorithm for finding the NSEC RR that proves that a given name
   is not covered by any applicable wildcard is similar but requires an
   extra step.  More precisely, the algorithm for finding the NSEC
   proving that no RRsets exist with the applicable wildcard name is
   precisely the same as the algorithm for finding the NSEC RR that
   proves that RRsets with any other owner name do not exist.
requirements.condition: An authoritative name server is finding the NSEC RR proving that no RRsets exist with the applicable wildcard name.
requirements.required_behavior: Find that NSEC RR using the same conceptual lookup algorithm used to prove that RRsets with any other owner name do not exist.
requirements.why_checkable: NSEC selection for an absent applicable wildcard name can be compared with ordinary absent-owner-name selection for the same target name.

requirements.quote:
The algorithm for finding the NSEC RR that proves that a given name
   is not covered by any applicable wildcard is similar but requires an
   extra step.  More precisely, the algorithm for finding the NSEC
   proving that no RRsets exist with the applicable wildcard name is
   precisely the same as the algorithm for finding the NSEC RR that
   proves that RRsets with any other owner name do not exist.  The part
   that's missing is a method of determining the name of the non-
   existent applicable wildcard.  In practice, this is easy, because the
   authoritative name server has already checked for the presence of
   precisely this wildcard name as part of step (1)(c) of the normal
   lookup algorithm described in Section 4.3.2 of [RFC1034].
requirements.condition: An authoritative name server is determining the nonexistent applicable wildcard name for an NSEC proof that a given name is not covered by an applicable wildcard.
requirements.required_behavior: Use as the applicable wildcard name precisely the wildcard name whose presence the authoritative name server already checked during step (1)(c) of the normal lookup algorithm referenced in RFC1034 Section 4.3.2.
requirements.why_checkable: The wildcard name used as the denial-proof lookup target can be compared with the wildcard candidate already checked during normal name lookup.
